evals.prompt: I have a Rectangle class with mutable width and height and setWidth/setHeight methods. I now need a Square type in the same system. What's the cleanest way to model Square given I already have Rectangle?
assertions: States that making Square extend/inherit from Rectangle violates the Liskov substitution principle
Recommends against Square subclassing Rectangle and instead proposes composition or separate/independent types (e.g. immutable shapes or a shared interface rather than a subclass)

evals.prompt: Two of my classes each have a handful of nearly identical helper methods. Should I pull those into a shared abstract base class so both can inherit them? Give me a concrete recommendation.
assertions: Advises NOT extracting a base class hierarchy yet and instead favors composition or a shared helper, noting a base class is premature with only two implementations
References the guidance that a base class should be extracted only once there are roughly three or more implementations / start flat

evals.prompt: Code review: a NonRemovableList subclass extends List but overrides its remove() method to throw UnsupportedOperationException because removal isn't allowed. Is this a good design? Name the problem.
assertions: Identifies this as the Refused Bequest smell and/or a Liskov substitution principle violation
Recommends replacing the inheritance with composition (wrapping/delegating to a List) rather than subclassing

evals.prompt: I'm writing a Java Money value class and I just added an equals() method so two Money instances with the same amount compare equal. I plan to use Money objects as keys in a HashMap. Anything else I need to do?
assertions: States that hashCode() must also be overridden to be consistent with equals(), otherwise HashMap/HashSet lookups break silently
